sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Disillusionment can challenge a particular promise without invalidating every good. Reconstruction may change an institutional affiliation, a role or a belief; none requires forced gratitude or immediate replacement certainty.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional Sol expected a certificate to produce belonging. After receiving it, no group contact followed. Sol still enjoys drawing small landscapes, has an already welcome Thursday meal with a friend and owes no further course fee. Sol questions the marketing promise, not whether every kind of learning has value. No traumatic event or acute crisis is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Separate failed expectation, supported facts and global interpretations. Choose one remaining good and a low-demand action, without claiming the disappointment was beneficial.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A group breaks one explicit promise. Someone concludes every possible community is unsafe. What can be challenged without denying the breach?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A meal or private drawing can retain its own value. Later fiction: Sol attends the meal and remains disappointed; companionship occurred, not a cure. Partial: name a remaining good without a feasible action. Incorrect: infer all relationships or learning are fraudulent. For an institution, examine specific governance/complaint evidence before affiliation decisions; for faith, compare authorized interpretations with a willing trusted adviser if desired; for role identity, try a reversible expression of the valued good. These are distinct inquiries, not compelled conversions.
criteria: The failed promise is stated specifically
A remaining good is not used to erase loss
Next steps fit the kind of disillusionment

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: The universal inference exceeds the supplied breach. Preserve the specific harm, appropriate boundaries and need for support while leaving other groups unknown. Joining a replacement group is optional, not proof of recovery.
